description: Importing Joshua's workout history from his Google Sheets ("Workout Progress - Upper Body / Lower Body / Core", exported as CSV). Each sheet is a grid: the first row is session dates (newest first), each later row an exercise, and each cell what was done that day, as ; -separated groups of weight, reps : 300lbs, 10 one set of 10 at 300 lbs 60lbs, 2x5 2 sets of 5 50lbs, 6,10 a set of 6, then a set of 10 3x8 bodyweight: 3 sets of 8 02:00:00 / 2x 30 seconds / 5x0:30 timed holds (Sheets turns 2:00 into 02:00:00) Anything else is read as far as it can be, and the cell's own text is kept in the workout's note so nothing is lost. This module only parses; scripts/import-sheets.js writes to the database.
content: sheetImport Importing Joshua's workout history from his Google Sheets ("Workout Progress - Upper Body / Lower Body / Core", exported as CSV). content: Globals --- Instance Methods A 'YYYY-MM-DD' date as a whole day number, so two dates are compared as calendar days, never as moments: a workout's date has no time of day, and new Date('YYYY-MM-DD') is midnight UTC, which in the evening west of UTC is already more than a day before the local "now" (21:30 in Toronto counted yesterday's workout as 2 days ago). Parameters - date Other Generates a menu with the provided index as the currently selected item. Parameters - tableRows (Array) - tableHeadings (Array) - tableClass (string) Returns - Object. Builds the add-exercise form's DOM structure. No event wiring here - see exercisePicker.js's own note on why that has to happen after this is attached into the real document and rendered. Primary and secondary are two separate multi-selects (rather than one picker with a per-muscle rank) - a real exercise's muscles split cleanly into those two buckets, and a plain multi-select needs no dynamic add/remove row UI to support picking several of each. Parameters - muscles (Array) — musclePriority()'s shape (every real muscle, not just priority ones) - becomes both selects' options Returns - Object Wires the form's submit button - see addExerciseForm's own note on timing. Parameters - form (Object) - onSubmit (function) — ({ name, description, primaryMuscleIds, secondaryMuscleIds }) = void Generates a menu with the provided index as the currently selected item. Parameters - currentIndex (number) Returns - DomItem Builds the muscle - exercise picker's DOM structure. No event wiring here - fullAddEventListener needs a complete parentItem chain up to the real document root (it throws otherwise), which a freshly-built, not-yet-attached DomItem doesn't have yet. Call wireExercisePickerEvents once this is attached into the real document and rendered. Parameters - priorityRows (Array) — musclePriority()'s shape, ordered by priority - becomes the muscle dropdown's options, top priority first Returns - Object Wires the picker's change events, once it's attached into the real document and rendered - see exercisePicker's own note on why this can't happen at construction time. Parameters - picker (Object) - onMuscleChange (function) — (muscleId: string) = void - onExerciseChange (function) — (exerciseId: string) = void Parameters - session (Object null) — getLastSession()'s shape, or null if never logged Returns - DomItem Builds the log-workout form's DOM structure. No event wiring here - see exercisePicker.js's own note on why that has to happen after this is attached into the real document and rendered. Returns - Object Reads the form's current field values, independent of which button triggered it. Parameters - form (Object) Wires the form's submit and update buttons - see logWorkoutForm's own note on timing. Parameters - form (Object) - onSubmit (function) — ({ weightEffort, sets, reps, note, date }) = void, logs a brand new entry - onUpdate (function) — ({ weightEffort, sets, reps, note, date }) = void, corrects the most recently shown entry Generates a table ranking muscles by how much they need attention right now. Parameters - priorityRows (Array) — musclePriority()'s shape: \[{ muscleId, name, daysSinceLastWorked, timesWorkedThisWeek, needsPriority }] Returns - Object. Generates a table for a workout plan. Returns - DomItem A date as 'YYYY-MM-DD' in the machine's own timezone - the shape every workout's date uses. Not toISOString().slice(0, 10): that's the UTC date, which is already tomorrow in the evening anywhere west of UTC (21:30 in Toronto is 01:30 UTC). Parameters - date — defaults to now Rank muscles by how much they need attention right now, from a real read of the database: every muscle (including ones never worked at all), and every workout row with its muscles already joined on (see workout()/musclePriority.test.js for the exact query shape this expects). A muscle needs priority once it's past its recovery window, or hasn't been worked often enough this week yet - whichever muscle has gone longest without being worked sorts first. Parameters - muscles — every row from read muscles - workoutsWithMuscles — every row from the workouts-joined-to-muscles query, each carrying a .muscles array (the muscles that workout's exercise worked) - today — injectable for testing; defaults to the real current time (only its local date counts) The app's reads, given the json-fs-query query and quote to run them with: Node's (workoutQueries.js, for the API server and the tests) or the browser build's (browserReads.js, for the page, which reads database/ from its own origin over fetch()). Reads need no server; only writes do. Parameters - jsonFsQuery (Object) Returns - Object A value that is the \ id of the exercise with this name, once it's inserted: exercises' ids are generated on insert (json-fs-query's auto replaces any \ id given), so rows refer to them through this. Parameters - name (string) Returns - function The rows every test database starts with: the app's original seed data (14 muscles, 3 exercises each linked to one muscle, and 6 workouts on 2024-06-02 and 2024-06-05). Fixed here, so tests never depend on the real database/, which changes with every workout logged. Build a test database at destination: every record the real database has, with the same fields and keys (read from its record files, so a schema change reaches the tests), holding only the given rows. Configures json-fs-query to use it. Parameters - destination (string) — The folder to create the test database in. - rows (Object.\ , optional, default: "seedRows") — The rows to insert, by record, in an order that keeps the foreign keys valid. - source (string, optional, default: "'database/'") — The real database whose schema is copied. Returns - Promise. — The inserted rows by record (with their generated ids). Log a new workout entry. Parameters - exerciseId - weightEffort - sets - reps - note - date — defaults to today (the local date, see localDate), in the same 'YYYY-MM-DD' shape the rest of the data uses - order — where this entry falls among others logged the same day (defaults to first) Update an existing workout entry - e.g. correcting the plan with what was actually done. Parameters - workoutId - changes — any subset of weightEffort/sets/reps/note to change Add a new exercise, with the muscles it works (primary/secondary, by whatever rank you give).
